title: The All-Star band and leaving for Pensacola
summary: His teen band under George Morris rehearsed together, took drummer Joe Wynn, and left for a Pensacola baseball park job in April 1924.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Where did you go to after Dave Perkins? Did you go to any other teachers?

Well, no. Like I said, this little, this band, they were all fellows older than me because I was just about 18, if I remember well. And they were all the trombone players named George Morris and the trombone players named Thomas Mack. And the clarinet player was named Edmund Washington.

And we used to rehearse around there and we used to go to the trombone house and rehearse. I was on 8 and Liberty and I had a cousin, Ray Fielder. And he was playing drum, but every Sunday, remember, we used to rehearse on them. And some fella came in town by the name of Joe Wynn, looking for a band, and they got in the word of it. And so they made a deal with him. And the only thing about the deal was this fella, Joe Wynn, played drum.

And there was a job in Pensacola and I was still going to school. So in order to take the job, we had to leave my cousin behind, you see. Oh, yeah. And he didn't like that so well, so we had promised him when we'd get over there and we'd get around and everything and everything. Well, we would get rid of this guy and then send for him, you see. For sure, we, my mother didn't want me to go. My father said, well, you better let him go because it looks like that's what he wants to be, a musician. So I was in ninth grade, I remember, 30, McDonald's 35 High School. That's around about April of 1924.

So we left. We went to Pensacola, Florida. And when we got there, we took up a piano player. I can't think of the woman's name right now. And we played for a doctor named. There was two fellas running a baseball park there. There was one, Dr. Burgundy, and the guy that was under Meatmark was named Mary and Long. It was sort of a corporation. They ran this baseball park with named Moore Castle Park. And they had a colored ball team. We used to play like Mobile and Montgomery all around that vicinity.
But did you always play guitar in the early days or did you play banjo as well?
